what: The four stages of the network, with the tensor shapes a real forward pass produced for a 40-ply game.

stages.name: Convolutional trunk
stages.role: Turns one board into a position vector.
stages.detail: Four convolution and batch-norm blocks with leaky ReLU and average pooling, run on every ply of the game at once. The board arrives as 12 planes of 8 by 8, one plane per piece type and color, and leaves as a 256-number summary.

stages.name: Bidirectional LSTM
stages.role: Reads the game as a sequence.
stages.detail: Three stacked bidirectional LSTM layers of hidden size 64. Each ply's input is the 256-number position summary with the standardized clock reading appended, so the input width is 257 and the output is 128, the two directions concatenated.

stages.name: Causal-cumulative attention
stages.role: Lets each move weight the moves before it.
stages.detail: Additive Bahdanau attention of dimension 64 over the LSTM output, masked so ply t attends only to plies 1 to t. Its context is added back to the LSTM output as a residual, so with attention switched off the forward pass is the baseline exactly. The per-ply weight the diagrams show is the mean weight each ply receives across all query positions.

stages.name: Rating head
stages.role: Produces two rating numbers per move.
stages.detail: A 128 to 32 linear layer with leaky ReLU and dropout, then a 32 to 2 linear layer. That last layer is the only place in the whole network where White and Black are separated, which is why the two estimates come out nearly identical.
